faq.q: Is April a good month for a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, April is a great month for a boat rental in Marbella, especially if you want to avoid the summer crowds. Air temperatures range from 18°C to 24°C, and sea temperatures are around 16–18°C. You'll get plenty of sunshine, though you should pack a light jacket for the breeze. Easter week is busier, so book early.

faq.q: What is the sea temperature in Marbella in April?
faq.a: The Mediterranean off Marbella in April averages 16–18°C. It's refreshing for a quick dip, but not ideal for long swims unless you're used to cooler water. If you're planning a swim stop, consider a boat with a swim platform, like the Azimut 58 Flybridge or the Ferretti 94.

faq.q: Which boats are best for Easter week in Marbella?
faq.a: For groups up to 12, the Mangusta 80 or Azimut 58 Flybridge offer plenty of space and comfort. The Mangusta 80 includes a free jet ski on charters of 4+ hours. For smaller groups, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 are budget-friendly options at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper and drinks.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance for Easter?
faq.a: Absolutely. Easter week is one of the busiest periods in Marbella. Boats like the Mangusta 80 and Ferretti 94 are often booked weeks ahead. We recommend reserving at least 2–3 weeks in advance, especially if you want a specific boat or a morning departure slot.

faq.q: What should I wear on a boat in April?
faq.a: Layers are key. Start with a light long-sleeve shirt and add a windproof jacket or fleece. The sun can be strong, so bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat. For swimming, a wetsuit or rash vest helps. Non-slip boat shoes are recommended, not flip-flops.

faq.q: Are there any weather risks in April?
faq.a: April can bring occasional showers and stronger winds, usually from the Levante (east) or Poniente (west). Our skippers monitor forecasts closely and will adjust the route or timing if needed. If a storm is forecast, we'll offer a reschedule or full refund, so you're covered.

faq.q: Can we still swim and do water sports in April?
faq.a: Yes, you can swim, though the water is brisk. Water sports like jet skiing (included on the Mangusta 80) are popular because you're moving fast and staying active. Paddleboarding is also possible if you have a wetsuit. For a warmer option, many boats have sun pads to relax on.

faq.q: What is the best time of day for an April charter?
faq.a: Midday to late afternoon (11:00–17:00) is ideal, as the sea breeze picks up and temperatures peak. Morning charters are calmer but cooler. Sunset charters (17:00–19:00) are magical but can be chilly – bring a jacket. We can tailor departure times to your preference.

Planning a Marbella boat rental in April 2037? Easter week falls early that year – Good Friday is 5 April – so expect a lively Puerto Banús and prime conditions for cruising the Costa del Sol. With air temperatures reaching 24°C and sea temperatures around 16–18°C, it's warm enough for sunbathing and a refreshing dip, but you'll want a light jacket for the breeze. April Weather in Marbella: What to Expect

April in Marbella is transitional: spring warmth is building, but the sea hasn't fully warmed up. Average highs are 20–24°C, with overnight lows around 12–14°C. You'll get around 8–9 hours of sunshine daily, and rainfall is moderate – typically 3–4 rainy days in the month. The water temperature is 16–18°C, so swimming is possible but invigorating.

Wind and Sea Conditions

The dominant winds are the Levante (east) and Poniente (west). Levante can bring choppier seas, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar, while Poniente is drier and calmer. In April, expect 10–15 knot breezes, which are manageable for most charters. Our skippers know the best sheltered anchorages, like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, to keep you comfortable.

Easter Week 2037: Key Dates and Crowds

Easter Sunday is 6 April 2037, with Semana Santa processions throughout the week (30 March – 6 April). Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina will be busy, and so will the water. Charter demand peaks on Good Friday and Easter Monday. If you're flexible, consider a mid-week charter (Tuesday–Thursday) for quieter seas and better availability.

Best Boats for April Charters

For groups of up to 12, the Mangusta 80 (24m) is a top pick – it includes a free jet ski on charters of 4+ hours, perfect for adrenaline on cooler days. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) offers a protected flybridge and spacious saloon, ideal if a shower passes. For smaller budgets, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 are excellent at €749 for 2 hours, or €2,299 for a full 8-hour day – both include skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks.

What's Included in Every Charter

All our charters depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs – just show up and enjoy. For larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86, pricing is on request via WhatsApp, so contact us for a tailored quote.

April Charter Itinerary Ideas

With 8–9 hours of daylight, you can plan a classic route: head east to Cabopino or west to Estepona. A popular half-day trip is to Cala del Faro for snorkelling, then lunch at a beach club. For a full day, go to Sotogrande and back, stopping at Cala Cortés. Always check the forecast with your skipper – they'll adjust to maximise sun and minimise chop.

Booking Tips for Easter 2037

Book at least 3 weeks ahead, especially for the Mangusta 80 or any yacht over 20m. Confirm your departure time – morning slots (10:00) are popular. If you're flexible, ask about last-minute deals. And remember: Easter falls early in 2037, so the water will be cooler than in May – pack a wetsuit if you plan to swim.
